analysis:
Examined three changes.

1) Gemma4TensorParallelRequestLoop.swift (head lines 49-172). The decode loop is refactored onto TensorParallelOneTokenLoop with one-step build-ahead via session.submitDecode. Pipelining is gated by `pipelines` (lines 66-69). A greedy request asking for logprobs is not pipelined, so the host-side collective cannot wait on a step built ahead. Tokens are still committed and published only after the agreed token is read (commit at 162-165). A step built past the end is evaluated but never committed or published, so there is no new plaintext or ciphertext egress on the provider-to-coordinator leg (T-008, TB-002). The E2E encryption path is not touched. Rank-0 logprobs are taken at build time (`built`, line 79-82) and kept per step. This avoids cross-step mixing of one request's sampler state, and I saw no cross-request or cross-tenant leakage. `withoutActuallyEscaping(check)` is used for the cancellation/deadline check closure (line 119). Cancel and deadline still reach `evaluate` (line 134), so T-010 cancellation is preserved from what is visible. The ordering of collectives across ranks, the stop-flag agreement (localStop, pagesRefused, stopKeep) and the final reconcile/exchange sit in TensorParallelOneTokenLoop, which is not supplied. A rank desynchronization there would be an availability or correctness risk (rank deadlock, T-010/T-029-like), not a confidentiality one. The `@TaskLocal buildsAhead` override is described as test-only, and I saw no product setter.

2) ClusterPlacementTool+Served.swift. It only passes the new serving and tensorAssistant fields from local planner files into setups. This is an offline CLI that reads local files, and there is no new trust boundary. The scope-by-build filter (servedScope) is unchanged. Whether serving/tensorAssistant participate in setup equality or build scoping lives in ClusterServedSpeedRecords.Setup, which is not supplied.

3) QwenLayerStageGenerationSchedule.swift line ~68. finish() now allows exactly one discarded decode forward on EOS. The check remains strict: it requires reason == .eos and a count of exactly 1, and selectedTokenCount == decodeForwardCount + 1 - discarded still holds. This loosens an integrity check in a narrow, documented way. It depends on the unsupplied QwenTensorParallelBatchDriver always producing exactly one discard on EOS.

No concrete security regression is found. Remaining questions concern the unsupplied TensorParallelOneTokenLoop and the session.submitDecode semantics.
